issues: Measurement integrity: no problems found. The diff reads no files and uses no network. It contains no hard-coded coordinates, and all randomness comes from the rng seeded by `seed`.

Correctness: no bug that makes the result meaningless. Every remove-and-reinsert candidate goes through clip and `_repair` before it is compared, so the returned packing is always repaired. `or best is None` makes sure at least one restart runs. The time check uses `process_time` against the same budget as the incumbent, so the risk of going over time is the same as before.

z does not quite match. The candidate mean is -2.63105, so the gain over the incumbent is 0.00305. With noise sd 0.0023, the standard error is 0.0023*sqrt(1/2+1/10) = 0.00178, which gives z ≈ 1.71, not the reported 1.751. Rounding of the shown values cannot fully explain the gap, so the harness may use a different variance estimate. The difference is small and does not change the provisional decision.
The evidence is weak: only 2 candidate runs and z ≈ 1.7, against a gain of about 0.003 that is close to the 0.0023 per-job noise. One more replicate would make the accept more trustworthy.
Minor point: when a reinsertion is rejected, the next try still removes the same smallest circle, just at a new random position. This is not a bug, but the search may be narrower than it could be.

After the random-restart phase, replace the remove-and-reinsert step with basin hopping: perturb all centres of the best packing with Gaussian noise (sigma 0.03), clip to the square, re-run SLSQP from that warm start, repair, and keep the result only if the sum of radii improves.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. The randomness comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. The only change is the starting radii, and the later repair step still makes the packing valid. The -0.125 offset equals sigma^2/2, so the average starting radius stays at INIT_RADIUS, as intended.
Possible small issue: lognormal draws can be larger than the radius bounds used in _optimise, if any. That only affects the starting point, and SLSQP or the repair step handles it.

Recomputed z: the candidate scores 0.0014 better than the incumbent. The standard error of the difference is 0.0023*sqrt(1/1+1/2) = 0.00282, so z ≈ 0.50. This is consistent with the harness value of 0.508; the gap comes from rounding of the shown values. The gain is within noise, and it rests on one candidate run, so rejecting is right.

records.description: Initialise each SLSQP restart's radii from a log-normal distribution with mean about 0.05 and sigma 0.5 (seeded by rng, clipped to a minimum of 0.01) instead of a constant 0.05.
Stop the random-restart phase early after 15 consecutive restarts fail to improve the best sum, handing the remaining time to the remove-and-reinsert basin-hopping phase from the incumbent.

In the remove-and-reinsert loop, pick the new centre of the removed circle from 500 uniform candidates by maximising the smaller of (distance to the nearest remaining circle edge) and (distance to the nearest wall), keeping its radius at 0.
Each random restart places k (6 to 12) centres exactly on the walls, with the rest uniform in the interior, to bias starts toward boundary-touching packings.

After the best packing is chosen, a new _grow helper visits circles in random order, twice over, and raises each radius to the largest value that keeps it inside the square and clear of all other circles, with the existing SHRINK margin kept.
Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9 so each solve uses about 27 s of its 30 s CPU budget, with no other change.
Before each free-radius SLSQP solve, first run a max-min SLSQP that maximises a common radius t with all radii equal to t, then warm-start the free-radius solve from those centres and t.

In the remove-and-reinsert loop, screen 6 random reinsertion positions of the smallest circle with a cheap analytic-gradient L-BFGS-B overlap-penalty minimisation at fixed radii, and send only the lowest-penalty candidate through the full SLSQP and repair.

Pruning the constraints by the starting distances (keep a pair only if its centres start closer than 2*max(r0)+0.1) can drop no-overlap constraints for pairs that move closer during SLSQP. The post-hoc repair shrinks radii, so the packing stays valid and the harness checks it exactly. This weakens the method but does not make the result meaningless; it may explain the lack of gain.
Raising the repair passes from 50 to 1000 is cheap (26x26 work per pass) and makes a valid final packing more likely; no time-limit risk.

Recomputed z: (-2.629 - (-2.6311)) / (0.0023*sqrt(1+1/2)) = 0.0021/0.00282 = +0.745 when subtracting the incumbent from the candidate. The harness's -0.743 is the same size with the opposite sign (improvements positive), with the small gap down to rounding. Not significant and slightly worse, so reject is right.

records.description: Sparse neighbour-pair constraints: each SLSQP call builds pair constraints only for centres closer than 2*max radius + 0.1, and the repair loop runs up to 1000 iterations so the all-pairs check still yields a valid packing.

In the remove-and-reinsert loop, fix the radii of a random 30 percent of circles (via SLSQP bounds (r, r)) for a first optimisation of centres and the other radii, then run a full free-radius _optimise starting from that result, accepting only if the repaired sum beats the incumbent.

After each accepted reinsertion, try a squeeze (scale by a factor in [0.97, 0.995]) and an expand (factor in [1.005, 1.03]) of all centres about (0.5, 0.5), re-optimise and repair both, and keep the better one if it beats the incumbent.
In the remove-and-reinsert loop, accept a worse packing with probability exp(delta/T), where T decays geometrically from 0.01 to 1e-4 over the loop, and always return the best packing seen.

Replace the uniform random start in each random restart with a concentric-ring layout (3 to 5 rings with random positive counts summing to n, evenly spaced centres with a random rotation per ring and Gaussian jitter of 0.02), leaving the rest of the restart phase unchanged.
Batch of 4 perturbed candidates per basin-hopping step, keeping the best if it beats the incumbent (not run).

After 10 consecutive non-improving reinsertion steps, apply a gravity kick (inward pull of the centres along a random direction with strength 0.02 to 0.05, radii scaled by 0.9, then re-solve and repair) and keep it only if it beats the current best.

issues: Recomputed z: the candidate's loss is 0.0002 worse than the incumbent's (-2.6309 vs -2.6311). The standard error is 0.0023*sqrt(1/1+1/2) ≈ 0.00282, so z ≈ -0.071. The harness's -0.065 differs only because the inputs are rounded, and the reject decision stands.
The candidate has only one run, so the comparison has little power. The difference is well inside the noise, and there is no evidence that the growth initialisation helps.
No integrity problems found. The diff has no file access and no hard-coded coordinates, and all randomness comes from the seeded rng.

No bug found that would make the result meaningless. _grow only produces a starting point. Overlaps that jitter creates mid-growth are clamped through max(...,0), and the final packing still goes through SLSQP and the existing repair step. 300 steps on 26x26 arrays costs almost nothing.
Minor: INIT_LOW and INIT_RADIUS may no longer be used in _solve_once. If nothing else uses them, delete them to keep the code simple.

Minor: calling this 'Lubachevsky-Stillinger style' overstates it. It is simple greedy inflation with decaying random jitter, not event-driven molecular dynamics. This is a wording issue, not a correctness one.

records.description: Before each random-restart SLSQP solve, grow the radii from zero over 300 steps (each radius grows by half the minimum pair gap or the wall distance, then centres are jittered with a shrinking Gaussian) and use that packing as the starting point.

Replace the uniform random initial centres in _solve_once with a greedy largest-hole build: each new centre is the best of 2000 seeded random candidates, scored by the minimum of its wall distance (clipped at 0.5) and its distance to the nearest existing centre, with all radii starting at INIT_RADIUS.

After the random-restart phase, keep a second elite packing and, every 5 reinsertion steps, build a child by exchanging circles across a random cut line between the two elites, then optimise and repair it and let it replace the worse elite if better.
Replace the sqrt pair-distance constraint in SLSQP with the smooth squared form (c_i - c_j)^2 summed minus (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0, which is valid because radii are nonnegative.

Before each random-restart SLSQP solve, pick the best of 2000 random centre sets after 30 vectorised 1/d^2 repulsion steps (scored by min pairwise distance and wall distance), and use it with uniform radii of half its minimum pair distance, capped at 0.1, as the start.

The NaN warnings come from divide-by-zero in _spread_start when clipped or random centres coincide, so the repulsion step produces NaN coordinates that propagate into the returned packing; adding a small epsilon to the squared distance removes the division by zero.

Alternate the random restarts between uniform-random initial centres and a jittered hexagonal lattice (random subset of lattice points scaled into the square, Gaussian sigma 0.02 jitter), keeping the radius initialisation unchanged.

Supply analytic gradients for the SLSQP objective and the full constraint Jacobian (pair, wall and radius rows) in _optimise, replacing finite differencing so each iteration is cheaper.
Replace the 4n wall inequality constraints with SLSQP bounds on centres [0,1] and radii [0,0.5] (not run: the idea changes the feasible set).
Each random restart overpacks n+3 circles from random starts, then repeatedly drops the smallest-radius circle and re-optimises until n remain, so only the pruned 26-circle packing is compared.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The new move swaps the centres of one of the 5 largest and one of the 5 smallest circles. With n=26 those two groups never overlap, so i != j. The swapped state then goes through the same _optimise, clip and existing accept/repair path as before. A swap that does not help is simply rejected.

Recomputed z: (inc - cand) / (0.0023 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = (-2.6311 + 2.6299) / 0.002817 = -0.426. The harness reports -0.417. The small gap is most likely rounding in the displayed means, and the sign is the same.
The candidate is worse than the incumbent by about 0.0012, which is less than one noise sd, and it rests on a single run. Rejecting it fits the numbers. The diff makes no claims that contradict them.

records.description: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, with probability 0.5 swap the centres of one of the 5 largest and one of the 5 smallest circles (radii kept), then re-optimise and accept only on improvement of the repaired radius sum.

In the random-restart phase, odd restarts draw initial radii from a 70/30 mixture of small (uniform 0.02 to 0.06) and large (uniform 0.08 to 0.12) circles, while even restarts keep the uniform INIT_RADIUS of 0.05, and the best packing across all restarts is kept.

Before the SLSQP polish in each random restart, run an L-BFGS-B penalty continuation (mu = 10, 100, 1000, 1e4) on -sum(r) plus squared overlap and boundary violations, and warm-start SLSQP from its result.

memo: Helped: slot 0 (remove-smallest-and-reinsert after a short random-restart phase) is the incumbent at -2.6311 (runs -2.6305, -2.6316; delta -0.0031). Several replicated variants sit near or below the incumbent but were rejected: slot 18 annealing acceptance (-2.6348/-2.6332), slot 4 Latin hypercube starts (-2.6343/-2.6335), slot 30 hex/uniform alternation (-2.6337/-2.6317), slot 34 multi-removal (-2.6334/-2.6313). Their deltas are within noise of slot 0 and may be worse or equal. Slot 32 analytic gradients (-2.6330, one run) and slot 7 log-normal radii (-2.6325, one run) are unreliable at noise sd 0.0023. Did not help: basin hopping (+0.0030), position screening (+0.0023), sparse constraints (+0.0021), ring starts (+0.0037), mirror starts (+0.0036), squeeze (+0.0015); most other tweaks about +-0.0002. Next: combine slot 0 with LHS starts, the slot 18 acceptance rule and analytic gradients (faster SLSQP), replicate at least twice, then add the slot 7 radii init. Avoid single-run conclusions.

incumbent.description: After a short random-restart phase, repeatedly delete the smallest circle, reinsert it at a uniform random position, re-optimise with SLSQP and repair, and keep the result only if the sum of radii improves.

backlog.spec: Supply the gradient of the objective (-sum of radii) and the Jacobian of the constraint vector analytically, passed as jac= and the constraint's jac entry, instead of letting SLSQP finite-difference them. Each pair constraint d_ij - r_i - r_j has known partials w.r.t. centres (unit vector u_ij = (c_i - c_j)/d_ij) and radii (-1). Boundary constraints have trivial partials. This cuts the per-iteration cost sharply, so more restarts fit in the same 24 s budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Instead of all n(n-1)/2 = 325 pair constraints, build pair constraints only for pairs whose centres are closer than a cutoff (e.g. 2*max radius + 0.1) at the start of each SLSQP call, and rebuild the list once after the first solve. Fewer constraints make SLSQP's QP subproblems much cheaper; a final check with all pairs guards validity.
backlog.title: Sparse neighbour-pair constraints

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, minimise -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, overlap)^2 + boundary violation^2) with L-BFGS-B for mu in an increasing sequence (e.g. 10, 100, 1000, 1e4). Use the result as the warm start for SLSQP. The penalty stage gives a cheap, well-conditioned basin estimate that SLSQP then polishes exactly.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call with scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-constr') using the same objective and inequality constraints wrapped in NonlinearConstraint(lb=0, ub=inf). Keep the restart loop unchanged. Compare final sum of radii on the same seeds; keep whichever method gives the higher mean.
backlog.title: trust-constr instead of SLSQP

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, freeze the centres and solve the linear programme maximise sum(r) subject to r_i + r_j <= d_ij for all pairs and r_i <= distance of c_i to each wall, using scipy.optimize.linprog (highs). This gives the optimal radii for those centres exactly and replaces the heuristic radius shrinking in _repair, so less sum is lost to repair.
backlog.title: Exact LP radius polish for fixed centres

backlog.spec: Pass centre coordinates as SLSQP bounds [0,1] and radii as bounds [0, 0.5] via the bounds argument, instead of the 4n wall inequality constraints in cons(). This shrinks the constraint vector from 325+26+104 to 325+26 and removes the wall-gradient work from each iteration, with no change to the feasible set.
backlog.title: Use bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: Write each pair constraint as (c_i - c_j)^2 summed minus (r_i + r_j)^2 >= 0 (valid when r_i + r_j >= 0) instead of using the square root. This removes the sqrt and its singular gradient when two centres nearly coincide, which is common early in SLSQP, and makes the constraint smooth everywhere.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints

backlog.spec: Tighten each pair and wall constraint by a small margin eps (e.g. 1e-7): require d_ij - r_i - r_j >= eps and r_i <= wall distance - eps. SLSQP then returns strictly feasible solutions, so the repair step rarely needs to shrink anything and the validity check in double precision holds without losing much sum.
backlog.title: Margin in pair constraints

backlog.spec: After an initial random-restart phase (about 30% of the time), repeatedly perturb the best packing's centres with Gaussian noise (sigma about 0.03), clip to the square, re-run SLSQP from that warm start, repair, and keep the result only if its sum of radii improves. Use the seed-driven rng for all noise.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Starting from the incumbent, delete the circle with the smallest radius, place it at a uniformly random position in the square, re-optimise with SLSQP, repair, and accept only if the sum improves. Repeat until the time budget is spent. Small circles are the least constrained, so moving them is the cheapest way to explore new topologies.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Solve with n+3 circles (e.g. 29) from random starts, then repeatedly drop the circle with the smallest radius and re-optimise until n circles remain. The extra circles give the optimiser slack to find better arrangements, and pruning keeps only the useful ones. Return the 26-circle packing with the largest sum.
backlog.title: Overpack and prune

backlog.spec: Alternate restarts between uniform-random initial centres and a hexagonal lattice of roughly n points scaled to fill the square, with random subsets chosen and Gaussian jitter (sigma about 0.02) added to each centre. Keep the radius initialisation unchanged. Lattice-like starts are close to the structure of good dense packings, so they begin the search in better basins.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-grid plus jitter initialisation

backlog.spec: Initialise radii from a log-normal distribution (mean about 0.05, sigma about 0.5, seeded by rng) instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS, then clip to a small positive minimum. Varied initial sizes break the symmetry of equal-radius starts and let SLSQP settle into arrangements with mixed circle sizes, which the optimum tends to use.
backlog.title: Log-normal initial radii

backlog.spec: For each restart, place a random number k (between 6 and 12) of the centres exactly on the four walls or in the corners, and place the rest uniformly at random in the interior. Optimal packings of squares contain many circles touching the boundary, so this biases starts toward a feasible structure.
backlog.title: Boundary-biased initial centres

backlog.spec: Generate initial centres with a Latin hypercube sample in [0.1, 0.9]^2 (one point per row and column stratum, seeded by rng) rather than independent uniform draws. Stratification gives more even coverage of the square, which lowers the chance that several restarts land in the same basin.
backlog.title: Latin hypercube initial centres

backlog.spec: First solve a max-min problem: maximise a common radius t subject to pair and wall constraints with all radii equal to t, using SLSQP. Then use the resulting centres and t as the warm start for the full free-radius SLSQP solve. The equal-radius stage gives a well-spread arrangement before the radii are allowed to differ.
backlog.title: Two-stage equal-then-free radii

backlog.spec: Generate half of the initial centres at random and mirror them across the main diagonal (c -> (y, x)), filling the remaining slots with random points on the diagonal or near it, so that the start is symmetric. Run the free SLSQP solve from this start, unconstrained afterwards. Symmetric starts sample a different family of arrangements than uniform starts.
backlog.title: Diagonal-symmetric initial layout

backlog.spec: Maintain an elite pool of the 5 best packings found so far. For each new restart, build a child by taking the circles whose centres lie left of a random vertical cut from one parent and the circles right of the cut from another, fix the count to n by adding or removing circles near the cut, then run SLSQP and repair. Keep the pool updated with the best results.
backlog.title: Elite crossover of packings

backlog.spec: Run many restarts with a short SLSQP budget (maxiter about 40). Keep the best quarter, re-run them with the full MAX_ITER, and keep the best quarter of those for a final full-length solve. This spends most of the time on starts that already look promising while still sampling broadly.
backlog.title: Successive halving over restarts

backlog.spec: Track how many consecutive restarts failed to improve the best sum. When that count exceeds a threshold (e.g. 15), switch the remaining time from random restarts to basin hopping from the incumbent. Otherwise continue random restarts. This avoids spending the whole budget on restarts that have stopped finding better basins.
backlog.title: Adaptive restart stopping and reallocation

backlog.spec: Call SLSQP repeatedly from its own output, each time with a fresh call, until the sum of radii improves by less than 1e-9 or 5 calls have run, with ftol set to 1e-12. A single SLSQP call often stops early at a non-converged point, so re-running it from the result squeezes out extra sum at little cost.
backlog.title: Iterate SLSQP to convergence

backlog.spec: Run the SLSQP solve in stages: first fix all radii at a small fraction (e.g. 0.6) of the initial value and optimise only the centres, then release radii to be free and re-optimise. Gradually letting radii grow gives the centres time to spread before the radii press against each other, which tends to find better arrangements.
backlog.title: Annealed radii schedule

backlog.spec: Set TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.9 so each solve uses 27 s of the 30 s CPU budget. The harness voids only calls above 45 s, so this leaves a safe margin while adding about 12 percent more restarts. Pair this with no other change to isolate the effect of the extra time.
backlog.title: Raise the time fraction to 0.9

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, add small random noise (sigma about 1e-3) to the centres and radii and re-run SLSQP once more, keeping the better of the two results. SLSQP can stall at saddle points or degenerate configurations with coincident constraints, and a small jitter moves the solution out of them.
backlog.title: Jitter re-solve to escape degenerate points

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, accept a new packing with a worse sum of radii with probability exp(-(old - new)/T), where T decays geometrically from about 0.01 to 1e-4 over the run. Always keep the best packing seen separately. Occasional acceptance of worse packings lets the search cross barriers between basins.
backlog.title: Metropolis acceptance in basin hopping

backlog.spec: At each basin-hopping step, generate B = 4 perturbed copies of the incumbent (different Gaussian moves or single-circle relocations), run a short SLSQP on each, and move to the best of the batch if it beats the incumbent. Taking the best of several cheap candidates raises the chance of an improvement per unit of CPU time.
backlog.title: Batch of candidate perturbations per step

backlog.spec: Run a population of 8 independent chains, each starting from a random packing. Advance every chain by one short SLSQP or basin-hopping step per round, and after every round replace the worst 2 chains with copies of the best chain plus a perturbation. Return the best packing found across all chains.
backlog.title: Lockstep population with greedy culling

backlog.spec: Replace the one-pair-at-a-time repair loop with a single pass: for every pair with positive overlap, shrink both radii by the same factor so that r_i + r_j equals the centre distance, then repeat the pass up to 5 times and finish with the wall clamp. Only if a violation remains, fall back to the existing loop. This keeps more radius sum after repair when SLSQP leaves small overlaps.
backlog.title: Pairwise tight repair

backlog.spec: After the best packing is chosen, visit circles in a random order and, for each, increase its radius to the largest value that keeps it inside the square and not overlapping any other circle, holding the others fixed. Repeat over the circles twice. This is cheap, always feasible, and recovers slack that the repair step leaves behind.
backlog.title: Greedy radius growth after selection

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres in _solve_once with a greedy build. Place circles one at a time: for each new circle, draw about 2000 candidate points uniformly in [0,1]^2, score each by its distance to the nearest existing centre and to the walls (clipped to a maximum of 0.5), and take the best candidate as the new centre. Give every circle the initial radius INIT_RADIUS. Pass the resulting centres and radii to _optimise as usual. Use the seed-driven rng for all candidate draws so runs stay reproducible.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-hole sequential seeding

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, draw a random weight w_i in [0.5, 1.5] for each circle and minimise -sum(w_i * r_i) instead of -sum(r_i) in _optimise. The constraints stay unchanged. Weights change which basin SLSQP falls into. After this solve, run one unweighted _optimise call from the resulting point to restore the true objective, then call _repair as before. The restart selection rule is unchanged.
backlog.title: Weighted-radius objective for basin diversification

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion phase, instead of reinserting only the smallest circle, pick a random disc of radius about 0.25 centred uniformly in the square. Every circle whose centre lies in that disc gets a fresh uniform random position inside the square and radius 0. Run _optimise on the full packing, clip, repair, and accept only if the sum of radii improves, as the current loop does. The disc centre and the rebuilt set are both drawn from rng.
backlog.title: Localised region destroy-and-rebuild

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, with probability 0.5 use a swap move instead of reinsertion. Pick one circle among the largest 5 and one among the smallest 5, exchange their centres while keeping each radius, and re-optimise with _optimise. Otherwise keep the existing remove-and-reinsert move. Accept only on improvement of the repaired radius sum, as before. The swap moves act as a cheap local change in the arrangement of sizes, and no new parameters are needed beyond the swap probability.
backlog.title: Radius-swap moves between unequal circles

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, generate K=6 candidate moves per step (each a reinsertion of the smallest circle at a random position). For each candidate, minimise a quadratic overlap penalty with L-BFGS-B on the centres with radii held fixed at their current values, which is cheap compared with SLSQP. Only the candidate with the lowest final penalty goes through the full _optimise and _repair. Accept it only if it improves the radius sum, as now. Keep K and the penalty weight as module constants.
backlog.title: Cheap penalty-energy screening of candidate moves

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion phase only, pass bounds to minimize: each centre coordinate is restricted to within 0.08 of its value at the start of the call (intersected with [0,1]), and each radius to [0, 0.3]. Keep the constraints unchanged. This keeps the local re-optimisation near the incumbent, so the solver can converge in fewer iterations and reach a deeper local optimum within the same MAX_ITER. The restart phase is unchanged. Add one module constant for the box half-width.
backlog.title: Move-limited SLSQP with box bounds around the current point

backlog.spec: Use the reinsertion loop as a dual search. Periodically (for example every 20 steps) solve the (n+1)-circle problem with _optimise, starting from the incumbent plus one extra circle placed at a random position with radius 0.05. Repair the result, then remove the circle whose removal leaves the largest repaired radius sum for n circles, and run _optimise and _repair on those n remaining circles. Accept only if the sum of radii beats the incumbent. This explores configurations that differ by one circle from the incumbent.
backlog.title: Solve n+1 circles then delete one

backlog.spec: Before the random-restart phase, with probability 0.5 build the initial layout by splitting the square into 2 or 3 vertical strips of equal width. Assign circles to strips in proportion to strip area, and place each strip's centres uniformly inside the strip with the initial radius. Run _optimise on the full problem from this layout. The other half of restarts keep the uniform random layout. This gives the optimiser structured starts with a mix of row-like arrangements.
backlog.title: Vertical strip decomposition for seeding

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, replace the uniform sample for the new centre of the removed circle with a hole search. Draw 500 uniform candidate points, score each by min over remaining centres of distance minus the remaining radius, and also by distance to the walls, and take the point with the largest score as the new centre. Keep the radius at 0 as now. Run _optimise and _repair as before. This is a targeted choice of the reinsertion spot, which the uniform draw does not make.
backlog.title: Hole-finding reinsertion position

backlog.spec: After each accepted reinsertion step, apply a small random jitter of standard deviation 0.01 to all centres, shrinking the jitter by a factor of 0.97 on each step that does not improve the incumbent and resetting it to 0.01 on success. Re-solve with _optimise, repair, and keep the result only if the sum of radii beats the incumbent. This is a stochastic kick whose size adapts to progress, so it is a different acceptance scheme from the existing pure-improvement rule.
backlog.title: Random active-set perturbation with decay

backlog.spec: For each random restart with n even, draw n/2 free centres uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW] and place their mirror images at (1-x, 1-y), so the packing is symmetric under 180-degree rotation about (0.5, 0.5). Give each pair a shared radius. Run SLSQP on this reduced problem (half the variables, with the pair and wall constraints written for the full set of circles), then unfreeze all variables and run one full _optimise polish from the symmetric result. Keep the best packing by sum of radii after _repair, as before. This halves the search dimension and is cheap to implement.
backlog.title: 180-degree rotational symmetry reduction

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random start with a concentric-ring start. Draw a random number of rings k in {3,4,5}, then draw ring counts m_1..m_k (outer to inner) with the total equal to n, using random positive integers that sum to n. Place the m_j centres evenly on a circle around (0.5, 0.5) of radius proportional to the ring index, with a random global rotation per ring and small Gaussian jitter of scale 0.02. Set the initial radii to 0.05 as before and pass the result to _optimise. Keep the rest of the random-restart phase unchanged. This gives structured starts that random uniform sampling rarely produces.
backlog.title: Ring-layer initial layout

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, generate a start by growth: place n random centres, start all radii at 0, and repeat about 300 steps. Each step, grow every radius toward the largest value that keeps it inside the walls and not overlapping any neighbour (using the current pair gaps, scaled by 0.5), then jitter every centre by a Gaussian of scale proportional to the remaining free space, shrinking the jitter geometrically. Use the rng seeded by seed for all randomness. The final centres and radii become x0 for _optimise. This is a physics-inspired compression that tends to find jammed, dense states that SLSQP from random points can miss. It is a bolder change, so it can be confined to the random-restart phase.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger style stochastic compression

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, before calling _optimise, choose a random 30 percent of circles and fix their radii at their current values by using a reduced variable vector for those indices (equivalently, set their radii as constants in the constraints). Optimise centres and the free radii for the rest, then run a second full _optimise with all radii free, starting from that result. Accept the new packing only if the sum after _repair beats the incumbent, as before. The point is to let the centres re-arrange around a partly fixed set of large circles, a regularisation of the joint search that changes which local optimum is reached.
backlog.title: Freeze-and-thaw radii subset

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, replace the choice i = argmin(r2) with a choice weighted by local crowding. For each circle compute the number of neighbours whose centre is within distance 2.2 times the mean radius, and pick the circle with the most neighbours among a random subset of 5 candidates (ties broken by smallest radius). Remove that circle and reinsert it at a random position as before. This targets the jammed region where a relocation is most likely to free space, instead of always the smallest circle. Keep all other steps unchanged.
backlog.title: Remove from the most crowded region

backlog.spec: Maintain 4 chains after the random-restart phase, each holding a packing. Chain k perturbs its packing by reinserting its smallest circle and, with probability p_k, jittering a random subset of centres by Gaussian noise of scale s_k, where s_k is geometric from 0.01 (cold) to 0.15 (hot). Each step, every chain proposes one perturbation, runs _optimise and _repair, and accepts with the Metropolis rule at a fixed temperature T_k tied to the chain index, using sum of radii as the energy. After every 10 steps, attempt to swap the states of adjacent chains with the standard exchange probability. Return the best packing found across all chains. This is a batch of coupled chains that can escape basins the single greedy loop cannot.
backlog.title: Parallel tempering over perturbation strength

backlog.spec: After each _optimise call in the remove-and-reinsert loop, identify the active contacts (pairs and walls with constraint value below 1e-7). Build the Jacobian of those active constraints with respect to all variables by finite differences, compute an orthonormal basis of its null space with numpy SVD, and take a random direction inside that null space with norm 0.02. Move the packing by this step, then re-run _optimise and _repair. Keep the candidate only if the sum of radii after repair beats the incumbent. Null-space moves keep the contacts intact to first order, so they explore the flat directions of the jammed configuration instead of random restarts.
backlog.title: Null-space kick at a jammed optimum

backlog.spec: Change the acceptance rule of the remove-and-reinsert loop from strict improvement to threshold accepting. Accept a candidate packing if its sum of radii after _repair is at least the incumbent's sum minus a threshold tau, where tau starts at 0.004 and decreases linearly to 0 over the loop. Always keep a separate copy of the best packing found so far, and return that copy at the end, so the loop may drift through slightly worse states without losing the best. Everything else stays the same, including the random-restart phase and the reinsertion move.
backlog.title: Threshold accepting in the reinsertion loop

backlog.spec: After each accepted improvement in the remove-and-reinsert loop, try a global perturbation: scale all centres about (0.5, 0.5) by a random factor drawn uniformly from [0.97, 0.995] (a squeeze), set radii to the repaired values, run _optimise, then _repair. Also try the reverse factor in [1.005, 1.03], clipped to the unit square. Accept the better of the two candidates if it beats the incumbent. This moves every circle at once and can unjam a packing that is locked against the walls, which single-circle reinsertion cannot do.
backlog.title: Squeeze-and-expand global rescale

backlog.spec: Before SLSQP, find a start that is spread out with a cheap proxy. Generate 2000 random candidate centre sets for the n circles (using rng), and for each one run 30 iterations of a repulsive gradient step that pushes pairs apart with a 1/d^2 force and keeps centres inside [0.05, 0.95]. Score each set by its minimum pairwise distance and by the minimum distance to the walls. Keep the best-scoring set as the centre part of x0 and set every radius to half the minimum pairwise distance of that set, clipped to be at most 0.1. Run _optimise from this start. This replaces uniform random centres with a distance-maximising start while keeping the rest of the restart phase intact.
backlog.title: Max-min-distance proxy start

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centres in _solve_once with structured seeds. Draw a random row count R in {4,5,6,7} and a random partition of 26 circles into R rows (each row 3 to 7 circles, sizes sampled at random). Place each row's centres at equal horizontal spacing across [0.1, 0.9], with rows equally spaced vertically across [0.1, 0.9], then add Gaussian jitter of scale 0.02 to every coordinate using the seeded rng. Initial radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. Keep the rest of the restart loop, SLSQP call, and repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Row-partition lattice seeds

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve and repair, identify the active constraints: pairs whose gap is below 1e-7 and wall constraints that are tight. If the number of active constraints is at least 2n+1 or so, solve the system of active equalities (pair distance = r_i + r_j, wall distances = r_i) with a few Gauss-Newton iterations on the 3n unknowns, using a least-squares solve from numpy. Accept the polished packing only if it passes the exact validity check after _repair and its radius sum is higher. This refines the optimum to machine precision and can recover small gains lost to SLSQP tolerance.
backlog.title: Active-contact Newton polish after SLSQP

backlog.spec: Rescale the decision variables before calling SLSQP so that centres and radii have comparable magnitudes and gradients are O(1). For example, optimise u = (c - 0.5) * 2 for centres and s = r * 10 for radii, and map back before the constraint evaluation. Also scale the objective to -sum(s)/10 so SLSQP's internal tolerances act on a normalised problem. Keep the constraint set and MAX_ITER unchanged. Compare the same number of restarts; the only change is the parametrisation inside _optimise.
backlog.title: Variable scaling for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Maintain an archive of local optima visited during the restart and reinsertion phases. Each packing gets a fingerprint: the sorted radii rounded to 2 decimals, concatenated with the sorted list of pairwise contact counts per circle. When a new candidate from reinsertion has a fingerprint within a small L1 distance of an archived one, skip the SLSQP re-solve and draw a new random reinsertion position instead. This stops the loop from cycling through the same basins and spends the time on fresh ones. Use only numpy; the archive is a Python list and the check is a vectorised comparison.
backlog.title: Novelty archive with basin fingerprints

backlog.spec: After each accepted packing in the reinsertion loop, detect rattlers: circles with fewer than 2 active contacts (pair gap under 1e-6 or wall tightness under 1e-6). For each rattler, in turn, remove it and reinsert it at the point of the free space that maximises the distance to all other circle boundaries, found by evaluating a 400-point uniform grid in [0,1]^2 with the seeded rng. Then run _optimise and _repair as usual. This targets loose circles directly instead of always removing the smallest radius, and it is a single change to the choice of index and position.
backlog.title: Rattler relocation

backlog.spec: Before any SLSQP call, generate K = 64 random starts at once as an array of shape (K, n, 2). Relax all of them together by projected gradient descent on a soft overlap energy sum over pairs of max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2 plus wall penalties, with the radii fixed at a common value that grows slowly from 0.05 to about 0.08. Use numpy broadcasting for the whole batch, about 300 iterations with step size 0.01. Then pass only the 4 lowest-energy configurations to SLSQP with free radii. Batch relaxation is cheap per start, so this replaces the purely random initial draw with a filtered pool.
backlog.title: Vectorised batch relaxation of many starts

backlog.spec: Treat the container as a square of side L instead of 1. Optimise the packing with centres in [0, L]^2 and L as a decision variable, with the objective maximising the radius sum minus a penalty of 0 when L is free. Start L at 1.25 and let SLSQP shrink it while keeping the constraints. Once the packing is found, rescale it to the unit square by dividing centres and radii by L, then run _repair. This sweeps the landscape from loose to tight, and it is a different path from the fixed-container solve used now.
backlog.title: Container-size homotopy

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centres with a sunflower spiral. For circle k = 0..n-1 set the polar radius rho = sqrt((k + 0.5) / n) and angle theta = k * pi * (3 - sqrt(5)), map to the square via centre = 0.5 + 0.4 * rho * (cos theta, sin theta) per axis, then add a random rotation of the whole arrangement and Gaussian jitter of scale 0.03 from the seeded rng. Keep INIT_RADIUS and the SLSQP solve unchanged. The spiral gives an evenly spread but non-lattice start, which differs from the lattice, hexagonal, and Latin-hypercube seeds already considered.
backlog.title: Spiral (Vogel) initial centres

backlog.spec: Within _optimise, run an outer loop of 4 rounds. In each round, first freeze the y-coordinates and radii and solve SLSQP over x-coordinates only, then freeze x and radii and solve over y-coordinates, and finally a full free solve with the result as the start. The block solves have half the variables and so converge faster and are less likely to stall at a degenerate point. Use the same pair and wall constraints; each block call simply passes the frozen values through the closure. Keep the final free solve so the output is still a joint local optimum.
backlog.title: Alternating block SLSQP over coordinates

backlog.spec: When the best packing has not improved for 10 consecutive reinsertion steps, apply a kick: pick a random direction and a strength of 0.02 to 0.05, move every centre by a small amount proportional to its distance from the square centre (pull inward along that direction), clip to [0,1], set all radii to 0.9 times their current value, and re-solve with _optimise followed by _repair. Accept the kicked result only if its radius sum beats the current best. This is a global shake that differs from the local reinsertion and basin hopping moves already tried.
backlog.title: Gravity kick at a jammed optimum

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call in _optimise with a custom log-barrier method. Maximise sum(r) + mu*sum(log(g_k(v))) over all constraint values g_k (pair gaps, wall gaps, r>=0) with scipy L-BFGS-B, using a numeric or analytic gradient. Start with mu=1e-2 and shrink mu by 0.2 for about 8 stages, warm-starting each stage from the previous one. Keep the iterate strictly feasible by backtracking when any g_k<=0. Finish with one SLSQP call from the barrier solution, so the final polish is still exact. The rest of solve (restarts, reinsertion loop, repair) stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Log-barrier interior-point continuation

backlog.spec: Add a sequential linear programming polish as an alternative to SLSQP for the reinsertion loop. At the current (c, r), linearise every pair-distance constraint d_ij - r_i - r_j >= 0 and the wall constraints around the current point. Solve scipy.optimize.linprog (highs) for a step that maximises sum(dr) subject to |dc|, |dr| <= delta. Accept the step if the true constraints (nonlinear) are satisfied or the objective improves, and otherwise shrink delta by half. Grow delta by 1.5 after successful steps. Run until delta < 1e-7 or the time is up, then apply _repair. Use this only in the reinsertion loop; keep SLSQP for the random restarts.
backlog.title: Sequential LP with trust region

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve in the random-restart phase, run a short deterministic decongestion pass. For 30 iterations, for each circle compute the vector sum of repulsion from all centres within distance 0.3, weighted by 1/d^2, add a small step of size 0.02 along that vector, then clip centres to [0.05, 0.95]. Keep the centre change if it lowers the total pairwise overlap energy sum(max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2) with r=0.05 for all circles, and reject it otherwise. This spreads out the clusters that random uniform starts often create, and it gives SLSQP a more even starting point.
backlog.title: Lloyd-style decongestion before SLSQP

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random start in _solve_once with a quadrant-based start. Split the square into a 2x2 grid of cells with random split points in [0.35, 0.65] on each axis. Allocate the 26 circles to the four cells in proportion to their cell areas, with the remainder going to random cells. Place each cell's centres uniformly inside that cell, shrunk by 0.03 from its edges. Set all radii to INIT_RADIUS and run the same SLSQP as before. This gives each start a different large-scale arrangement from the uniform start, and it is cheap to implement.
backlog.title: Quadrant decomposition seeding

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, instead of removing only the smallest circle, remove k in {1,2,3} circles per step, chosen as the k smallest radii (k is drawn uniformly each step). Reset each removed circle to a uniform random centre in [0,1]^2 with radius 0. Run the same _optimise and _repair, and accept the new packing only if its sum of radii is larger. Keep the rest of the solve function unchanged. This widens the neighbourhood in each step, so the loop can move several small circles at once.
backlog.title: Multi-circle removal and reinsertion

backlog.spec: In solve, after the random-restart phase, keep the three best distinct packings (ranked by sum of radii, skipping any whose sum is within 1e-6 of one already kept). In the reinsertion loop, cycle through these three elites in turn: each step takes the next elite, applies one remove-smallest-and-reinsert move, and updates that elite if the move improves it. Use the same time budget as before. This spreads the search over three basins instead of one, so a single unlucky basin does not take up the whole reinsertion phase.
backlog.title: Round-robin over top-3 elite packings

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, after removing the smallest circle and placing it at a random position, also perturb its k=4 nearest neighbours. For each neighbour j, add Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.5*r_j to its centre, then clip the centre to [0,1]^2. Set the neighbour's radius to 0.9 times its current value so SLSQP has room to move. Run the same _optimise and _repair, and accept only if the sum of radii improves. This kick scales with each circle's size, so the moves stay in the same region of the square.
backlog.title: Radius-proportional neighbour kick

backlog.spec: In the reinsertion loop, keep a list of the positions where the removed circle was reinserted in previous steps that did not improve the packing, together with the radius of the removed circle. When choosing a new position for the smallest circle, draw 200 uniform candidate points in [0,1]^2 and discard any candidate within 0.08 of a stored failed site. Take the candidate with the largest distance to its nearest centre among the remaining points. Clear the tabu list whenever an improvement is accepted. This steers reinsertion toward unexplored holes and avoids repeating the same unsuccessful moves.
backlog.title: Tabu memory of failed reinsertion sites

backlog.spec: Add a second start generator used in the random-restart phase on alternate restarts. Pick a random rectangular lattice of about 26 points: choose rows and columns among (4,7),(5,6),(6,5),(7,4), with a random row offset of half a spacing on every other row (a hexagonal-like stagger). Scale the lattice to span [0.1,0.9] in x and y with a random aspect jitter of up to 10 percent, then add Gaussian noise of standard deviation 0.01 to every coordinate. Keep the first 26 points, set radii to INIT_RADIUS, and run the same SLSQP call. This adds structured starts that the uniform-random generator rarely produces, while keeping the rest of the algorithm the same.
backlog.title: Stretched-lattice anisotropic start

backlog.spec: When the reinsertion loop has two elite packings A and B, produce a child by choosing a random line through the square. Take the circles of A whose centres lie on one side of the line and the circles of B on the other side, then adjust the count to exactly n by adding or removing circles nearest the line. Radii of the child come from the parent they were copied from. Run _optimise and _repair on the child, and replace the worse parent in the elite pair if the child is better. Run one child attempt for every 5 reinsertion steps, so most of the budget still goes to the existing move.
backlog.title: Cut-line exchange between two elites

backlog.spec: Replace the remove-and-reinsert loop with a (1+lambda) evolution strategy over the centre coordinates. Each generation draws lambda=6 children by adding Gaussian noise (sigma per generation) to the incumbent centres, then computes radii for each child with _repair on the current centres (no SLSQP). Keep the child with the largest radius sum if it beats the parent. Adapt sigma with the 1/5 success rule: multiply by 1.2 after a success, by 0.9 otherwise, clamped to [1e-3, 0.1]. Every 20 generations, run _optimise on the incumbent to polish it with SLSQP and keep the result if it is better. The random-restart phase is unchanged.
backlog.title: Evolution-strategy search over centres with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Keep the top two packings from the random-restart phase. Before crossover, align the second packing to the first with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment on the matrix of pairwise centre distances, so that circle indices correspond. Build a child by taking the centres and radii of the first elite for circles in one half-plane (x < a random cut x0 drawn from [0.3, 0.7]) and the aligned second elite for the rest. Repair the child, run _optimise on it, and then repair again. Keep it if its radius sum beats the incumbent. Use this crossover as an extra move alongside remove-and-reinsert, chosen with probability 0.3.
backlog.title: Elite alignment and crossover via assignment

backlog.spec: Instead of random starts at n=26, grow the packing from small size. Start with k=4 circles at random, optimise with _optimise, then insert one new circle at the centre of the largest empty region (sample 2000 random points and pick the one with the largest distance to all centres and walls) with radius 0. Re-optimise with _optimise. Repeat until n circles are placed. Use this growth path for a share of the restarts (about half of the random-restart phase, with different seeds for the insertion sample). Keep the best complete packing by radius sum as the start for the remove-and-reinsert loop.
backlog.title: Incremental growth from k to n circles with warm starts

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert phase, have three move operators: (a) remove the smallest circle and reinsert it at a random point, as now; (b) remove a random circle and reinsert it at a random point; (c) swap the centres of two random circles of different radii. At each step choose the operator by UCB1 over the running mean of the improvement it achieved (score = improvement in radius sum, 0 if none), with exploration constant 0.5 and an initial pull of each operator once. Apply the chosen move, run _optimise, repair, and keep it if the radius sum improves. Log per-operator statistics only in local variables.
backlog.title: UCB bandit over perturbation operators

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random initial centres in _solve_once with Bridson Poisson-disc samples in [0.05, 0.95]^2. Choose the minimum spacing d so that about 26 points fit, for example by a bisection on d over Bridson runs with the same rng (target 26 to 30 accepted points, trim extra points at random). Use INIT_RADIUS for the radii as now. This produces evenly spread starts with no clustering, while still varying with the seed. The rest of the restart logic is unchanged.
backlog.title: Poisson-disc starts with a radius-tuned spacing

backlog.spec: Track the displacement vector of the last accepted improvement in the remove-and-reinsert loop, meaning the change in the centre array from the old incumbent to the new one. At each later step, with probability 0.5, build a candidate by applying the previous accepted displacement scaled by a factor drawn uniformly from [1.0, 2.0] to the current incumbent, then repair and run _optimise. Otherwise use the usual reinsertion move. Clip centres to [0, 1] before repair. If the extrapolated move fails, fall back to the usual move in the next step.
backlog.title: Extrapolate successful moves

backlog.spec: In each random restart, draw a single cap value R_cap uniformly from [0.08, 0.2] and add the constraint r_i <= R_cap for all circles inside _optimise, implemented by clipping the bounds of the radius variables through the SLSQP inequality list (append R_cap - r for all i). Use the capped optimum only as a starting point: after the capped solve, run _optimise again with no cap, starting from its output, then repair. The cap forces the optimiser to spread circle sizes differently in each restart, which varies the basin found for each seed.
backlog.title: Random radius caps during early restarts

backlog.spec: Change the decision variables of _optimise so that the radii are r_i = exp(t_i) and the optimiser works on the 2n centre coordinates plus the n log-radii t_i. The objective becomes minus the sum of exp(t_i), and the constraints are the same with r_i replaced by exp(t_i). The initial log-radii are log(INIT_RADIUS). This keeps radii positive without the r >= 0 constraints and changes the curvature of the problem, so SLSQP may escape some degenerate points. Convert back to radii after the solve and keep the repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Logarithmic radius parametrisation

backlog.spec: In _optimise, add a penalty term to the objective with weight lambda = 0.05 that pulls each centre towards the centroid of all centres: subtract lambda times the squared distance from the centre array to its mean. Use this penalised objective for the first solve of each random restart only. Then run the standard _optimise objective starting from the result, so the final optimum is the true sum-of-radii optimum. The pull encourages compact early layouts with less wasted space near the boundary, and the second stage removes the bias.
backlog.title: Centroid-pull regularisation in early SLSQP

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, accept a candidate when its radius sum is at least the incumbent's minus 1e-9, not only when it is strictly larger. Keep the best packing seen so far in a separate variable, and return that best packing at the end. This lets the search drift across equal-sum plateaus, which occur when rattler circles move freely, and the best-so-far copy guarantees the returned value never drops below the best seen.
backlog.title: Plateau-accepting reinsertion moves

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, do not fix the kick size. Keep a multiplicative step factor s (start 1.0) and track the fraction of accepted reinsertions over a sliding window of 20 steps. If the window acceptance is above 0.2, multiply s by 1.1; if below 0.05, multiply s by 0.9; clamp s to [0.2, 3.0]. The kick moves the smallest circle to a uniform point in [0,1]^2 by mixing it with its current centre: c_new = c + s * (u - c) with u uniform, then clip to [0,1]. Everything else (SLSQP re-solve, repair, acceptance if sum improves) is unchanged. Use only the seed-derived rng.
backlog.title: Adaptive kick strength by acceptance rate

backlog.spec: Add a second move type to the remove-and-reinsert loop. With probability 0.5, pick a random circle whose centre lies within r of a wall (a wall-touching circle), and slide it along that wall to a uniform random position on the wall segment, keeping its radius at the old value so the SLSQP re-solve starts from a nearby point. Otherwise use the existing smallest-circle reinsertion. The move is accepted only through the existing sum-of-radii comparison. This is a single self-contained branch in the loop; no other code changes.
backlog.title: Edge-slide move for wall-hugging circles

backlog.spec: Run two independent remove-and-reinsert chains, each started from its own best packing found in a random-restart phase of half the restart time. Alternate chains in blocks of 10 reinsertion steps. Every 50 steps, the chain with the lower sum copies the other chain's best packing (migration), replacing its current state. Return the best packing over both chains at the end. Each chain uses its own rng child stream derived from seed so the run is reproducible.
backlog.title: Two-island model with periodic migration

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centres in _solve_once with Voronoi incentres. Draw k = n random seed points uniformly in [0,1]^2, compute the Voronoi cells restricted to the unit square by sampling a fine grid (e.g. 200 by 200 points) and assigning each grid point to its nearest seed, then set each centre to the mean of its assigned grid points (one Lloyd relaxation step). Add a small uniform jitter of 0.01 and clip to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. The radii initialisation and SLSQP call stay as they are. This gives roughly evenly spread but irregular starts, different from LHS and hex grids.
backlog.title: Voronoi incentre seeding for random starts

backlog.spec: Replace the single SLSQP call in _optimise with an outer augmented-Lagrangian loop. Keep the same constraints, but move the pair, wall and nonnegativity constraints into a penalty term: L = -sum(r) + sum_k (mu/2) * max(0, lambda_k/mu - g_k)^2 with multipliers lambda_k initialised to zero, where g_k >= 0 is each constraint value. Minimise L with L-BFGS-B over the stacked variables (centres and radii, with box bounds for centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5]). After each inner solve, update lambda_k = max(0, lambda_k - mu * g_k) and increase mu by 2x while it is below 1e4. Use 6 outer iterations. Finish with the existing repair step.
backlog.title: Augmented Lagrangian outer loop around the radius problem

backlog.spec: In the remove-and-reinsert loop, keep a memory list of past tried (site, gain) pairs, where gain is the change in sum of radii after the reinsertion re-solve. Before each reinsertion, draw 300 uniform candidate sites. For each candidate, predict its gain as the distance-weighted average of the gains of the 5 nearest remembered sites (inverse-distance weight, with a prior of 0 gain when memory is empty). Pick the candidate with the highest predicted gain, with probability 0.7; otherwise use a uniform random site. After the re-solve, append (site, gain) to memory and cap memory at 200 entries by dropping the oldest.
backlog.title: Surrogate-guided reinsertion site selection

backlog.spec: For each random-restart SLSQP solve, first tighten the wall constraints so each circle must stay inside [m, 1-m] with m = 0.02, while the pair constraints stay exact. Solve, then rerun the same SLSQP with m = 0 starting from that solution. Keep only the second result for scoring. This pushes the early solve away from boundary degeneracies and lets the second solve reach a different, often better, contact pattern. The change lives entirely inside _optimise, with an optional margin argument that defaults to 0.
backlog.title: Wall-margin homotopy in the first solve

backlog.spec: Split the post-restart budget into alternating epochs of 4 seconds of process time. Odd epochs run the existing remove-and-reinsert loop with the current move. Even epochs run an exploitation sweep: take the current best packing and run SLSQP from it with maxiter raised to 500 and a tighter SLSQP tolerance (ftol 1e-12), then repair. Keep whichever packing has the larger sum at the end of each epoch. The epoch lengths and the number of epochs are the only new settings and are derived from the time budget so the total stays inside the 80 percent limit.
backlog.title: Epoch-based exploration and exploitation schedule

backlog.spec: In the random-restart phase, alternate two kinds of starts. On even restarts, use the current INIT_RADIUS of 0.05 for every circle. On odd restarts, draw the initial radii from a two-class mixture: each circle is in the small class with probability 0.7 and gets radius uniform in [0.02, 0.06], or in the large class with probability 0.3 and gets radius uniform in [0.08, 0.12]. Centres stay uniform random as before. Both kinds go through the same SLSQP and repair path, and the best sum across all restarts is kept. This diversifies the basins reached early, which the remove-and-reinsert phase then refines.
backlog.title: Mixed-scale restarts: alternate large-radius and small-radius starts

backlog.spec: Inside _optimise, run SLSQP twice. The first pass uses the existing constraints with a loose SLSQP ftol of 1e-4 and maxiter 60 to get near a basin cheaply. The second pass restarts from that output with ftol 1e-10 and maxiter 200. Before the second pass, drop any pair constraint whose centre distance exceeds 0.5 for that call only (sparse-pair pruning is applied only for the first pass, so the second pass keeps all pairs). Keep the same return format. This trims wasted SLSQP iterations on far-apart pairs during the cheap phase.
backlog.title: Two-stage tolerance SLSQP with a loose first pass
